content_voiceover: This NCCN table lays out cytogenetic risk stratification for B-ALL, and you should be able to sort any karyotype into good or poor risk on sight. Good risk includes hyperdiploidy with fifty-one to sixty-five chromosomes, especially when trisomies of chromosomes four, ten, and seventeen are present together, and the translocation twelve;twenty-one producing ETV6-RUNX1. Poor risk is a longer, high-yield list: hypodiploidy under forty-four chromosomes, KMT2A rearrangements including translocation four;eleven, any IGH translocation, the Philadelphia chromosome translocation nine;twenty-two producing BCR-ABL1, which was defined as high risk in the pre-TKI era, and complex karyotype with five or more abnormalities. Ph-like or BCR-ABL1-like ALL is its own poor-risk category, subdivided into JAK-STAT pathway lesions like CRLF2, EPOR, and JAK rearrangements, ABL-class fusions involving ABL1, ABL2, PDGFRA, PDGFRB, or FGFR, and other kinase fusions like NTRK, FLT3, LYN, and PTK2B. Round out the poor-risk list with intrachromosomal amplification of chromosome twenty-one, translocation seventeen;nineteen producing TCF3-HLF, and IKZF1 alterations.
keypoints: Poor risk: hypodiploidy <44, KMT2A rearranged, BCR-ABL1
Poor risk: Ph-like ALL (JAK-STAT, ABL-class, other kinase fusions)
Poor risk: complex karyotype, iAMP21, TCF3-HLF, IKZF1 alterations
keypoint_voiceover: Two good-risk entities to memorize: hyperdiploidy, especially with trisomy four, ten, and seventeen, and ETV6-RUNX1. Everything else on this slide is poor risk, hypodiploidy, KMT2A rearrangements, Philadelphia chromosome, complex karyotype, Ph-like ALL with its JAK-STAT or ABL-class fusions, iAMP21, TCF3-HLF, and IKZF1 alterations.
